emotional_core: The moment you realize your analysis is invisible if the chart doesn't communicate — technical skill is necessary, but presentation is what gets heard in the room.
visual_metaphor: A before/after split — the same Titanic data shown as a default gray matplotlib chart on one side and a clean styled seaborn chart on the other: identical data, completely different story told
key_quotes: Visualization is where your analysis either lands or disappears.
Your charts will get judged before your model does.
The shift: from 'how do I make this chart' to 'what does this chart need to say.'

story_frames.visual: A person at a laptop, proud of their work — cut to a meeting room where people squint at a projected gray chart with tiny, unreadable text
Close-up of default matplotlib output: gray background, box border on all sides, small fonts, cluttered tick marks
story_frames.text: This is what 72 DPI looks like.

story_frames.visual: Same chart after sns.set_theme() — white background, subtle gridlines, no top or right border, readable font sizes
Five chart thumbnail previews arranged in a clean grid, each labeled: histplot, scatterplot, barplot, heatmap, boxplot
A 2×2 grid of four Titanic charts — survival by class, age distribution, fare by class, survival by sex — all consistent styling
Zoomed comparison of the same PNG at 72 DPI (left, blurry text) vs 300 DPI (right, crisp and sharp) — obvious difference at this scale
Person presenting to a small group pointing at a clean, well-labeled multi-panel chart on screen — audience engaged, no confusion, conversation happening
